units.function: Comprehensive relational service tests for Paperclip Pipeline invariants: idempotent ingest, optimistic concurrency, leases, transition/blocker/parent graphs, rollups, notifications, suggestions, automation dispatch/retry/provenance, workspace propagation and destructive retry cleanup.
units.dependencyDirection: PipelineActor commands enter pipelineService, which coordinates Postgres pipeline/case/event/link tables with issue, routine, heartbeat and workspace services. System-generated comments/issues carry dependency and automation context; routine execution state projects back into automation ledgers and case lifecycle.
units.keyDataModels: Pipeline/stage/transition; case key/version/parent/depth/terminal counters/workspaceRef/lease; blocker DAG; event and actor/run provenance; issue link and system notification; suggestion; routine and automation execution ledger keyed by trigger; automation attempt lineage; project/workspace configuration; retired case/reason and linked issue cleanup.
units.lifecycle: Create a versioned workflow and idempotently ingest cases; claim and mutate under lease/version fences; resolve dependency/parent graphs; roll terminal state upward; trigger system notifications or automatic parent movement; dispatch stage-entry routine exactly once per event; recover a failed dispatch idempotently; validate tenant/workspace references; optionally retire earlier automation output before a fresh attempt.
units.testAssessment: The 32 scenarios are strong design evidence for transactional invariants, graph safety, event attribution and failure recovery. Notable strengths include one-winner concurrent transitions, no event on stale/no-op mutation, lease expiry events, cycle/depth guards, per-item batch isolation, one-time rollup signals, trigger-ledger retry idempotency, untrusted-content marking and cross-tenant routine revalidation at execution. All 32 were skipped locally due unavailable embedded Postgres, so runtime behavior is unverified here. Missing are authorization for ordinary users and destructive retry, lease fencing tokens under long work, transaction/outbox crash points, multi-process retry races, cancel/backoff/dead-letter, immutable template versions, secrets tests, data/evidence contracts, human review qualifications and migration/rollback/performance tests.
units.designRationale: Provide robust workflow orchestration above issues while tolerating retries, concurrent operators, evolving automation configuration and hierarchical/dependent work without duplicating executions or corrupting rollups.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs FDE-configurable workflows and reliable Agent Boss orchestration, but all automated and destructive lifecycle decisions must remain subordinate to explicit human responsibility, permission/data contracts and evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT this as a leading reference for workflow mechanics: stable case keys, optimistic versions, lease events, DAG/depth validation, material-change detection, bounded idempotent trigger ledgers, attempt lineage, untrusted-content labels, tenant revalidation and explicit retry cleanup. Company OS should use immutable template versions plus migrations, durable command/outbox IDs, lease fencing, retry budgets/cancel/dead-letter and policy-evaluated compensation. Bind cases to Work and ResponsibilityContract; bind automation attempts to Connector capability, permission/data snapshots, model/secret references and attestations; bind review and destructive retry to qualified human decisions and exact digests. Never let an unqualified system transition silently override a human lease.
units.responsibilityConflict: A system child-completion transition can clear a human-held lease, and a generic userActor can invoke destructive retry cleanup that retires/cancels earlier Agent work. Neither is shown bound to accountable-human authority, responsibility contract, evidence review, exact action digest or affected-data scope. Automation dispatch creates work for an Agent from stage configuration alone.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: optimistic concurrency has an explicit one-winner test; stale/no-op mutations do not emit misleading events; leases and expiry are recorded; blocker/parent cycles and depth are bounded; cross-Company routines are rejected again at execution; generated Agent context is marked untrusted; crash retry is idempotent for the tested trigger; workspace scope is validated. CRITICAL responsibility risk: system auto-advance clears a human lease without an approval/responsibility check. HIGH destructive-authorization gap: retry cleanup can retire descendants and cancel linked work with no tested role/capability or human approval. HIGH automation durability gap: no outbox crash matrix, multi-worker race, cancel, backoff or dead-letter coverage. HIGH secret/data gap: despite a secret-related history commit, this unit proves no scoped secret delivery, redaction, data authorization/export or evidence handling. MEDIUM idempotency semantics: duplicate caseKey silently preserves the original payload, which needs explicit conflict/update policy. MEDIUM notification risk: system comments propagate upstream IDs/content without a tested disclosure policy. TEST GAP: all database-backed scenarios were skipped locally.
